clinicalReview: Required before activation in Epic. Not the standard of care.
title: Fever Without Localizing Signs, 0-60 Days
mission: Walk fever without a source in infants from birth through 60 days, taking the youngest infants first.
checkpoints: Confirm age, gestation of at least 35 weeks, and the temperature definition in the standard.
Split the workup at the age cut the PDF uses. The youngest neonates stay on the higher-intensity branch.
Stop for birth gestation under 35 weeks, for bronchiolitis at the ages the standard names, for a toxic or septic appearance, and for immunocompromise.
mayPropose: Unsigned laboratory, culture, and treatment orders quoted from the age branch.
cardSummary: TCH fever standard for infants 0 to 60 days may apply. Use the age branch in the PDF.

population.inclusion: Age 0-60 days (Infants ≥35 weeks gestation); Neonates and infants without underlying conditions; Actual rectal temp ≥100.4F (38C) OR reported temp (axillary or rectal) of ≥100.4F (38C) in any time during the past 24 hours; Neonates aged ≤21 days with bronchiolitis; Neonates and infants (0-60 days) with respiratory viruses including COVID-19
population.exclusion: History of prematurity with gestational age at birth less than 35 weeks; Infants aged ≥22 days with bronchiolitis; Underlying conditions that affect immunity or may otherwise increase risk of SBI; Toxic/Septic appearance; Receiving antibiotic treatment for FWLS; Routine vaccinations given within the previous 48 hours; Presenting with seizures; Requiring intensive care management; Identified focus of infection (e.g., cellulitis, acute otitis media in infants >28 days old)

source.publisher: Texas Children's Hospital Evidence-Based Outcomes Center
source.pdf: clinical-standards/25 Fever Without Localizing Signs 0-60 Days.pdf
